tool_summary: A shell builtin that replaces the current shell process with the specified command, rather than forking a child process. Used bare (with only redirections) it also permanently redirects the shell's own file descriptors.
platform_notes: exec is a POSIX-required shell builtin, behavior consistent across sh/bash/zsh/dash. Like eval, it is typically only visible to commandant as part of a larger shell invocation rather than standalone.

rules.description: Replaces the current shell process image with the given command; the shell does not resume afterward. If used in a script or session an agent expects to continue running in, this can silently terminate the intended control flow rather than simply running a command and returning.
rules.reversible_note: The original shell process is gone once replaced; there is no return to it.

rules.description: Bare exec with only redirection operators and no command (e.g. exec > file 2>&1) permanently redirects the shell's own stdout/stderr/stdin for the remainder of the session or script, rather than executing a new program.
